title: The Creation of the World
summary: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth over six days — light, sky, land, stars, living creatures, and finally man and woman — resting on the seventh day and declaring everything very good.
keyVerse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. — Genesis 1:1

title: The Fall of Adam and Eve
summary: Tempted by the serpent, Eve and then Adam ate the forbidden fruit from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. God confronted them, pronounced judgement, and expelled them from the Garden of Eden — the origin of sin and death entering the world.
keyVerse: For God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil. — Genesis 3:5

title: Noah and the Great Flood
summary: God saw the wickedness of humanity and chose the righteous Noah to build an ark. Noah, his family, and two of every creature survived a great flood. When the waters receded, God established a covenant with Noah, placing a rainbow in the sky as a sign.
keyVerse: I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth. — Genesis 9:13

title: Abraham and Isaac
summary: God tested Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice his beloved son Isaac on Mount Moriah. Abraham obeyed in faith, and at the last moment God provided a ram in place of Isaac, declaring Abraham's faith proven. A powerful foreshadowing of Christ's sacrifice.
keyVerse: Abraham reasoned that God could even raise the dead, and so in a manner of speaking he did receive Isaac back from death. — Hebrews 11:19

title: Moses and the Burning Bush
summary: While tending flocks on Mount Horeb, Moses saw a bush that burned but was not consumed. From it, God spoke, revealing himself as 'I AM WHO I AM,' and commissioned Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egyptian slavery.
keyVerse: I am who I am. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'I am has sent me to you.' — Exodus 3:14

title: The Ten Plagues and the Exodus
summary: God sent ten devastating plagues upon Egypt — including locusts, darkness, and the death of the firstborn — to compel Pharaoh to release the Israelites. The final plague was averted by the blood of the Passover lamb, and Moses led the people through the parted Red Sea.
keyVerse: When I see the blood, I will pass over you. — Exodus 12:13

title: David and Goliath
summary: The giant Philistine warrior Goliath taunted Israel's army for forty days. Young shepherd David, armed only with a sling and five stones and trusting in the Lord, stepped forward and struck Goliath dead with a single stone, routing the Philistines.
keyVerse: You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the Lord Almighty. — 1 Samuel 17:45

title: Elijah and the Prophets of Baal
summary: The prophet Elijah challenged 450 prophets of Baal to a contest on Mount Carmel to prove which God was real. Despite hours of prayer by the Baal prophets, nothing happened. When Elijah prayed, God's fire consumed the offering, the altar, and even the water. The people fell down crying, 'The Lord — he is God!'
keyVerse: Answer me, Lord, answer me, so these people will know that you, Lord, are God. — 1 Kings 18:37

title: Jonah and the Whale
summary: God called Jonah to preach repentance to Nineveh, but Jonah fled on a ship. A great storm arose and Jonah was thrown overboard, swallowed by a great fish for three days before being spat out. He went to Nineveh, the city repented, and God showed mercy — teaching Jonah about divine compassion.
keyVerse: From inside the fish Jonah prayed to the Lord his God. — Jonah 2:1

title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
summary: Daniel, an Israelite exile, served faithfully under King Darius but was thrown into a lions' den for refusing to stop praying to God. He spent the night unharmed among the lions, and the king, overjoyed, declared the God of Daniel to be the living God.
keyVerse: My God sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions. — Daniel 6:22

title: The Story of Job
summary: Job was a righteous and prosperous man who lost everything — his wealth, children, and health — through satanic testing. Despite immense suffering and pressure from his friends to confess sin, Job maintained his integrity. God ultimately restored Job's fortunes doubly and spoke to him from a whirlwind.
keyVerse: Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him. — Job 13:15

title: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
summary: Three young Israelites refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue and were thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter than usual. The king saw four figures walking unharmed in the fire. They emerged without a single hair singed, and the king praised the God of Israel.
keyVerse: If we are thrown into the blazing furnace, the God we serve is able to deliver us. — Daniel 3:17

title: Ruth and Naomi
summary: After the death of her husband, the Moabite woman Ruth refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi, declaring, 'Where you go I will go.' Through her faithfulness and hard work, she came to marry Boaz, a kinsman-redeemer, becoming an ancestor of King David and Jesus.
keyVerse: Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God. — Ruth 1:16

title: The Annunciation and Birth of Jesus
summary: The angel Gabriel appeared to the Virgin Mary and announced she would conceive the Son of God by the Holy Spirit. Jesus was born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger, as there was no room at the inn. Angels announced his birth to shepherds, who came to worship him.
keyVerse: For nothing will be impossible with God. — Luke 1:37

title: The Baptism of Jesus
summary: Jesus came to John the Baptist at the Jordan River to be baptised. As he came out of the water, the heavens opened, the Spirit descended like a dove, and the voice of the Father declared, 'This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.'
keyVerse: This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased. — Matthew 3:17

title: The Temptation of Jesus
summary: Immediately after his baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert where he fasted forty days and was tempted three times by the devil — to turn stones to bread, to throw himself from the Temple, and to receive all the kingdoms of the world. Jesus resisted each temptation with Scripture.
keyVerse: Away from me, Satan! For it is written: 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.' — Matthew 4:10

title: The Sermon on the Mount
summary: Jesus delivered his greatest teaching from a hillside, including the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, and commands on love, forgiveness, anxiety, and judging others. The crowds were amazed because he taught as one who had authority.
keyVerse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. — Matthew 5:8

title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
summary: A vast crowd followed Jesus. With only five loaves and two fish from a boy's lunch, Jesus gave thanks, broke the bread, and distributed it to more than five thousand people. After everyone had eaten their fill, twelve baskets of leftovers were collected.
keyVerse: Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. — John 6:11

title: The Transfiguration
summary: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain where his appearance was transformed — his face shining like the sun, his clothes radiant white. Moses and Elijah appeared with him. A bright cloud overshadowed them and God's voice declared, 'This is my Son, whom I love; listen to him!'
keyVerse: His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as the light. — Matthew 17:2

title: The Raising of Lazarus
summary: Lazarus, a friend of Jesus, fell ill and died before Jesus arrived in Bethany. At the tomb, Jesus wept — the shortest verse in the Bible. Then he called out, 'Lazarus, come out!' and the dead man walked out still bound in his grave clothes, revealing Jesus as the Resurrection and the Life.
keyVerse: I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die. — John 11:25

title: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
summary: A younger son demanded his inheritance early, squandered it in reckless living, and ended up feeding pigs. Coming to his senses, he returned home expecting to be a servant. Instead his father ran to him, embraced him, and threw a great celebration — the greatest parable of God's forgiving love.
keyVerse: But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son. — Luke 15:20

title: The Good Samaritan
summary: A man beaten by robbers lay dying on the road. A priest and a Levite passed by. A Samaritan — despised by Jews — stopped, bandaged his wounds, carried him to an inn, and paid for his care. Jesus used this story to answer 'Who is my neighbour?' and to teach active, costly compassion.
keyVerse: Go and do likewise. — Luke 10:37

title: The Last Supper
summary: On the night before his crucifixion, Jesus gathered with his twelve apostles, took bread and wine, gave thanks, and declared them to be his body and blood — instituting the Eucharist. He washed his disciples' feet and foretold that one among them would betray him.
keyVerse: This is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me. — Luke 22:19

title: The Agony in the Garden
summary: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus fell on his face and prayed intensely, sweating drops like blood, begging the Father to remove the cup of suffering if it were his will — but ultimately surrendering in trust. The disciples slept. Judas arrived with soldiers to betray him.
keyVerse: Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me; yet not my will, but yours be done. — Luke 22:42

title: The Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, bearing a crown of thorns. He spoke seven last words from the cross and died at three o'clock. Darkness covered the land, the temple veil tore in two, and the earth shook. A soldier confirmed his death with a spear. He was buried in a rich man's tomb.
keyVerse: It is finished. — John 19:30

title: The Resurrection of Jesus
summary: On the first day of the week, women went to Jesus' tomb and found the stone rolled away. An angel announced, 'He is not here; he has risen!' Mary Magdalene encountered the risen Jesus, who sent her to tell the disciples. Jesus appeared to them repeatedly over forty days.
keyVerse: He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. — Matthew 28:6

title: The Road to Emmaus
summary: Two disciples walked to Emmaus, downcast about Jesus' death. A stranger joined them and explained the Scriptures. When they reached the village and sat at table, he broke the bread — and their eyes were opened and they recognised it was Jesus, who then vanished. They rushed back to Jerusalem to tell the eleven.
keyVerse: Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us? — Luke 24:32

title: Pentecost and the Gift of the Holy Spirit
summary: Fifty days after the Resurrection, the disciples were gathered in Jerusalem. Suddenly a sound like a rushing wind filled the house; tongues of fire rested on each of them and they were filled with the Holy Spirit, speaking in other languages. Peter preached boldly and three thousand people were baptised that day — the birth of the Church.
keyVerse: When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. — Acts 2:1

title: The Conversion of Saint Paul
summary: Saul of Tarsus was a zealous persecutor of Christians, travelling to Damascus to arrest believers. On the road, a blinding light struck him down and he heard the voice of Jesus: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?' He was led blind into Damascus, fasted three days, and was healed and baptised — becoming Paul, the Apostle to the Gentiles.
keyVerse: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? — Acts 9:4

title: The Vision of Revelation
summary: The Apostle John, exiled on the island of Patmos, received a series of dramatic visions from God about the end of time. Christ appeared in dazzling glory, the church is called to persevere, and the climax is a new creation — a new heaven and a new earth — where God dwells with humanity and all suffering is ended forever.
keyVerse: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain. — Revelation 21:4
